To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of phylogenetic profiles to identify orthologs is not reliable.

the use of phylogenetic profiles in conjunction with hierarchical multi label classification (HMCL) provides a new and promising approach for the functional annotation of genes, and that this method can be successfully applied to the functional annotation of ortholog groups of genes.

(1) the phylogenetic profiling approach can be used to identify genes with similar functions; (2) a new phylogenetic profiling method, OrthoPhy, can be used to predict the function of a gene; and (3) the method can also be applied to identify genes that have a similar function to a given gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to identify the biological functions of genes based on their phylogenetic occurrence patterns.
the development of methods for the functional annotation of gene orthologous groups.
the development of new algorithms for the analysis of large-scale data from high-throughput experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genes having similar occurrence patterns in the phylogenetically profiled organisms have similar functions.
the phylogenetic profiling method is a useful tool in the field of comparative genomics.
phylogenetic profiling has the potential to identify novel gene functions, but that its use as an alternative method to traditional functional annotation is limited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phylogenetic profiles are used to predict the functions of the genes.

we have developed and applied a new approach to functional annotation, which is based on a hierarchical classification of orthologous gene groups, and which is able to predict functional information on a large scale, with high accuracy and with low redundancy.
we are trying to predict gene functions from the occurrence pattern of a gene in a set of organisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the functional annotations of genes are highly dependent on their phylogenetic profile.
the functional information contained in a phylogenetic profile can be exploited by a hierarchical machine learning approach to provide a functional annotation for the orthologous groups.
the functional annotation of orthologs can be improved by combining the phylogenetic profiling method with a machine learning approach.
